headline: July 13: Tarique Rahman to visit Barishal
summary: The BNP Secretary General is scheduled to visit the southern district to engage with party workers and local leaders.
details: BNP Secretary General Tarique Rahman is scheduled to visit Barishal on July 13.
The visit is part of his ongoing efforts to strengthen party organization and coordinate with regional leaders.
Local party members and supporters are preparing for the visit, expecting guidance on the party's future political strategy.

headline: HSC exams postponed in Chattogram, Rangamati and Cox's Bazar due to floods
summary: Severe rainfall and flooding in the three districts have forced the Inter Education Board Coordination Committee to reschedule the exams.
details: The Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations scheduled for Wednesday, July 8, have been postponed in Chattogram, Rangamati, and Cox's Bazar districts due to severe flooding.

An order signed by Professor Syed Aktaruzzaman, President of the Inter Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the decision for Cox's Bazar late Tuesday night, following similar orders for Chattogram and Rangamati.
Professor Aktaruzzaman stated that the postponed exams in these affected areas will be conducted later using separate question papers to maintain fairness.
The decision comes as Chattogram city experienced record-breaking rainfall, with 394 mm of rain recorded in 24 hours ending Tuesday evening—the highest single-day July rainfall in 43 years.
Heavy rains have also caused widespread waterlogging and flooding in Rangamati and Cox's Bazar, making it difficult for students to reach examination centers.
Exams in other education boards and other districts under the Chattogram Education Board, including Bandarban and Khagrachari, will proceed as scheduled.
caption:
Record-breaking rain and floods have forced the postponement of HSC exams in three districts.

The Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations scheduled for Wednesday, July 8, have been postponed in Chattogram, Rangamati, and Cox's Bazar districts due to severe flooding.

An order signed by Professor Syed Aktaruzzaman, President of the Inter Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the decision for Cox's Bazar late Tuesday night, following similar orders for Chattogram and Rangamati.

Professor Aktaruzzaman stated that the postponed exams in these affected areas will be conducted later using separate question papers to maintain fairness.

The decision comes as Chattogram city experienced record-breaking rainfall, with 394 mm of rain recorded in 24 hours ending Tuesday evening—the highest single-day July rainfall in 43 years.

Heavy rains have also caused widespread waterlogging and flooding in Rangamati and Cox's Bazar, making it difficult for students to reach examination centers.

Exams in other education boards and other districts under the Chattogram Education Board, including Bandarban and Khagrachari, will proceed as scheduled.
